agent: text wave, reader G (how a message reaches the player)
question: What each key of a messagetypes.txt entry does; PostMessage read whole; the popup windows, their text, buttons, placement and stacking; the log; the map text; how $VARIABLE$s are filled; the categories; where the player's settings are kept.

addresses.name: PostMessage_CMessageHandler
addresses.no_signature: A 0x78-byte CMessage passed by value between the receiver and nothing: handler [ebp+8], receiver [ebp+0xC], callback [ebp+0x10], the message [ebp+0x14], ret 0x84. The by-value struct is why no ordinary signature is written, as for PostMessage.
addresses.comment: **PostMessage<CMessageHandler>** - one of twelve instantiations of one template, the one with **91 direct callers**, read as identical to PostMessage (0x110A50) apart from the receiver type. The twelve differ only in the class T whose member function the message calls back (CMessageDialog<T>, CFunctionMessage<T>): the ten whose pointer-to-member is 4 bytes take (handler, T* receiver, callback, message by value) and end `ret 0x84`; CProvince's and CInGameIdler's, whose pointers-to-member are 8 bytes, put the callback pair after the message and end `ret 0x88`. Every one runs the same steps: nothing under g_NoPopups or with the handler disabled (+0x30); `Bad messagetype` for a null type; popup or pausepopup -> a dialog (CombatStartPopup for the six *ATTACK* names, else DefaultPopup for popup_kind 0, ElectionResultPopup for 3, none otherwise) and, single player only, a CPauseGame; onmap -> ShowMessageMapText; log -> CInGameIdler::AddMessageToLog. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-messageshow.md, section 2.
addresses.evidence: The instance's first call after the 'DefaultPopup' string is 0x435360, which writes CMessageDialog<CMessageHandler>'s table (RTTI); ends `ret 0x84` at 0x434C7B. A byte scan of all twelve bodies finds the same compares - +0xC, +0xD, +0xE once each and +0x10 twice on the type - in every one. Wrong if any instance branched on a type field the others do not; the scan says none does.

addresses.name: PostMessage
addresses.no_signature: The third of five arguments is a 0x78 byte object passed by value. Naming it would need a type for the message, which is only known field by field; the frame is in the comment, which is what a caller needs.
addresses.comment:
**PostMessage<CProvince> - shows a message**: pops it up, puts it on the map, logs it, according to its CMessageType. One of twelve instantiations of one template (the others are PostMessage_<T>); this one calls back a CProvince member.

`ret 0x88`, five arguments:

    +0x08  the handler (GetMessageHandler)
    +0x0C  the receiver of the callback - for CCountry::ShatterUnit the province
    +0x10  the message, 0x78 bytes **by value**
    +0x88  the callback: a pointer to a CProvince member, `bool (CProvince::*)(CMessage*)`,
    +0x8C  and its this-adjustment (0) - 8 bytes because CProvince's pointers-to-member are

The pair is **not a popup builder**: at every raise site it is CProvince::SelectBattleForMessage (0xA6040), the action of the popup's second button and of a click on the log line. In order: (1) g_NoPopups set -> nothing at all, no popup, no map text, no log line; (2) no in-game screen, or the handler's enabled byte (+0x30) clear -> nothing; (3) a null type -> `Bad messagetype` to the game log (messagehandler.h); (4) popup (+0xE) or pausepopup (+0x10): the type's name is one of ATTACKTHEM, ATTACKUS, AIRATTACKTHEM, AIRATTACKUS, NAVALATTACKTHEM, NAVALATTACKUS -> a CombatStartPopup dialog; otherwise popup_kind (+0x30) 0 -> DefaultPopup, 3 -> ElectionResultPopup, anything else -> no dialog; the dialog (0x180 bytes, built by 0x512EA0 with the message copied in) is added to the screen's dialog list (CEU3Idler::AddDialog). Then, in the same branch, **if the game is single player** (screen +0x68 clear), the type has pausepopup and the screen's slot 95 answers false, a CPauseGame(local player, 1) command is posted through the session's channel; (5) onmap (+0xC): ShowMessageMapText; (6) log (+0xD): a CFunctionMessage<CProvince> (0x90 bytes, 0x512260) where the callback is set, else a plain copy (CMessage::CopyTo), handed to CInGameIdler::AddMessageToLog (screen slot 36). It does **not** test that the message is for the player - every raise site does that before building it. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-messageshow.md, section 2.
addresses.evidence: Read whole off the listing 0x510A50-0x511464. Wrong if the callback were a builder: the dialog's own constructor calls the text builders directly (0x512FF5, 0x513003), and 0xA6040's body walks CProvince +0x2EC (combats) and centres the map - see its entry.
addresses.revises: The comment called the +0x88 pair 'the popup builder' and +0x0C 'the province'; the pair is a pointer-to-member callback and +0x0C its receiver, and the order of the six branches, the pause and the handler's enabled byte were not recorded.

addresses.name: CProvince::SelectBattleForMessage
addresses.comment: **The 'Goto' of a province's message: selects a battle in the province and centres the map on it.** The callback every CCountry::ShatterUnit-style raise passes to PostMessage (as a pointer to CProvince member, `mov esi, 0x4A6040`). `this` is the province the post was given; it walks the province's combats (CProvince +0x2EC, count +0x2F4): for a message whose type is AIRATTACKTHEM or AIRATTACKUS it takes the first combat whose CCombat::GetKind (slot 11) is 3, an air battle; for any other type simply the first. With one: screen slot 46 (clears the selection and closes the orders view), slot 38 with the combat's CSelectable (+8), CentreOnProvince(combat->province (+0x18)), and answers true. With no combat (or none of kind 3) it answers false. Called from the popup's DeclineButton (MessageDialog_PressGoto) - **the popup stays open when it answers true and closes when false** - and from a left click on the message's log line (CFunctionMessage slot 2). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-messageshow.md, sections 3 and 4.
addresses.evidence: Read whole, 0x4A6040 to `ret 4` at 0x4A62CD and the false exit at 0x4A62D5. +0x2EC is recorded as CProvince::combats and slot 11 as CCombat::GetKind with 3 = air (CCombatManager::CreateCombat's table). Wrong if `this` were the popup: the callers MessageDialog_PressGoto_MemberPtr8 (0x4505C0) and CFunctionMessage<CProvince> slot 2 (0x512330) call through the stored receiver, which PostMessage was handed at +0x0C.
addresses.revises: Was MessagePopupCallback, 'likely', with `this` taken for the popup and the purpose unknown. It is a CProvince member - the action of the second popup button and of a log click - and the name says what it does.

addresses.name: CMessageHandler::FindType
addresses.comment:
**A message type by name.** Forwards to the lookup at 0x299AC0 - the handler into eax, the name as a stack argument - and calls it a second time on the way out, which is what its result comes from.

**A name the registry does not hold does not come back null**: it logs `Failed to find message type: <name>` from messagehandler.cpp and returns GetNullMessageType() - a CNullMessageType named `NULL_MESSAGE` with the constructor's defaults: log on, everything else off, category 5 (cat_other). So a misspelt or undeclared type is still posted, as a log line whose text is the key NULL_MESSAGE_LOG (which no localisation table defines), dated like any other.
addresses.evidence: The miss path ends `call 0x69A8D0` (GetNullMessageType), whose result is the singleton 0x1A85614 built by 0x69A870 with `NULL_MESSAGE`, +8 = 5, +0xC = 0x100 (log byte +0xD = 1) and vftable 0x15D00FC (CNullMessageType). Wrong if 0x69A8D0 could answer null - it allocates on first use and returns the global.
addresses.revises: The comment said a miss 'returns null'. It returns the NULL_MESSAGE type, which logs.

addresses.name: BuildMessagePopupText
addresses.comment:
**Fills a message popup (popup_kind 0: DefaultPopup and CombatStartPopup)**, called once from each 4-byte CMessageDialog<T> constructor - ten callers; the 8-byte templates have their own copy, BuildMessagePopupText_MemberPtr8. The popup's window is +4, its message +0x6C (type +0x8C, variables +0x90). In order:

1. The settings glue (+0x144, right click -> MessageDialog_OpenSettingWindow) is attached to the window's background element (window +0x238) and to AgreeButton, DeclineButton and CenterOK.
2. Texts `<TYPE>_HEADER` and `<TYPE>_1`..`_6`, and for every variable of the message a replacement `$KEY$` -> GetText(value), i.e. **the value is itself looked up as a localisation key** and shows as itself only where no key matches. A variable named ATTDETAIL, DEFDETAIL, ATTTOTAL or DEFTOTAL also sets Line_left_1, Line_right_1, Line_left_2, Line_right_2 (where the window has them) to its raw value, its first §W turned to §b.
3. Header = the rendered _HEADER with its **first** `§W` replaced by `§b`; Line1..Line6 = each rendered line with **every** `§W` replaced by `§b`. A text that renders to exactly `*` renders as empty (CInternationalizedText::Render).
4. Layout: y starts at Header's y plus its drawn height; for i = 1..6, a line whose text is empty is skipped, else it is moved to y + 15 for Line2 (popup_textline_dist_two) or y + 0 (popup_textline_dist, y 0) and y grows by its drawn height. CombatStartPopup's combatstart_divider and the four Line_left/right lines follow. The background is resized to height y + 70 (popup_bottom_button_pos.y) + 50 (popup_textline_dist.**x**), and the three buttons are put at that height less 70.
5. Buttons by the type's `option` (+0x34): **no** -> AgreeButton and DeclineButton hidden, CenterOK shown with `<TYPE>_BTN1` and the dialog's close observer; **yes** -> CenterOK hidden, AgreeButton `<TYPE>_BTN2` (closes), DeclineButton `<TYPE>_BTN3`, which - where the post had a callback - runs it (MessageDialog_PressGoto) instead of closing.
6. Shields: LeftShield the message's first country (+0x34) and RightShield its second (+0x3C); with only one, both shields show it; with neither, they are left as the .gui has them.
7. Placement: the handler's cascade counter (+0x2C) is stepped and wraps from 11 to 0; the dialog goes 10 px x that counter right and down of its base position, clamped (a coordinate whose window would cross the screen's right or bottom edge is set to the screen size less 10), plus 40 px down.
8. Window slot 44 (slot 11 for the four EU3 leftovers WECARDINALBRIBE, WEFCARDINABRIBE, CURIACONTROLLER, CARDINALBRIBE).

See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-messageshow.md, section 3.
addresses.evidence: Read off the listing 0x4355B0-0x4383xx and the decompilation; the §W/§b order from 0x4366C4-0x43673C (find 0x15B6700 '§W', replace with 0x15B66FC '§b'); the layout from 0x4371D7-0x4373CF; the height from 0x437674-0x4376ED. Wrong if the callers were not dialog constructors: all ten are the 4-byte CMessageDialog<T> constructors (e.g. 0xA0D0C0), each calling it when popup_kind is 0.
addresses.revises: The comment had the popup's +0x144 as 'the element it hands to a virtual' and the run as 'from the popup's own update'; +0x144 is the right-click settings observer, and it runs once, from the dialog's constructor. The text, layout, buttons, shields and placement were not recorded.

addresses.name: CInternationalizedText::Render
addresses.signature: Hoi3CString* __thiscall CInternationalizedText::Render(CInternationalizedText* this@ECX, Hoi3CString* out@ESI, CTextRenderColours colours@stack:4) @EAX
addresses.comment: **A text object to characters.** `thiscall` on the object with sixteen bytes of colour settings pushed by value (`ret 0x10`), and the built string handed back in **esi** - the same register trick as the key in CInternationalizedText::Replace. It writes the length and capacity over whatever the out string held, so it must be given an empty one. **A text that comes out as exactly `*` is handed back empty** (compared with the one-character string 0x15BE4C4 at VA 0xA82E98): that is how a message line written `*` in the localisation disappears, everywhere a text is rendered and not only in popups. The name is BiceLib's.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x682E40-0x682F1C: the entry is rendered into a temporary by 0xA84E20, compared byte for byte with '*' (0x15BE4C4), and on equality the out string is assigned '' (0x15B4945) instead of the temporary. Wrong if the compare were a prefix test - it walks to the terminator of both strings.
addresses.revises: Adds the `*` rule; the rest of the comment is unchanged.

addresses.name: g_NoPopups
addresses.comment: **The `nopopup` console cheat.** One byte, toggled at VA 0x44194F ('Blocking all popups' / 'Stopped blocking all popups'). While set, FireEvent gives the local player's own events to the AI's weighted choice instead of a window, and **every message post does nothing at all** - it is the first test in all twelve PostMessage instantiations, before the popup, the map text and the log line, so the cheat empties the log as well as the popups.
addresses.evidence: `cmp byte ptr [0x1A8554F], bl; jne <exit>` is the first test after the frame in each of the twelve PostMessage_<T> bodies, jumping to the message's destructor. Wrong if any branch of a post ran before that test - none does.
addresses.revises: Said the event-message helper posts nothing; every message post does nothing, including the log line.

addresses.name: CMessageHandler::SaveCustomTypes
addresses.comment: **Writes messagetypes_custom.txt**: every registered type, in the registry's order, as `NAME =` and the type's own Save (CMessageType::SaveContents: log, onmap, popup, idle, option, pausepopup, categories).
